name: rgr-routing
name_note: Deliberately NOT named e2e-red-* (D-22). selfcheck-red.mjs auto-discovers e2e-red-* siblings and its crux 2 bans 13 state-claim tokens in prompts, but this corpus MUST carry test-state facts by design: D-03 exists precisely because routing has to IGNORE them, so a case like c4 ('nothing failing yet') is CORRECT and would hard-fail that ban. Naming the suite outside the discovered namespace is what keeps both invariants true and leaves selfcheck-red.mjs byte-unchanged. check-evals.mjs clause 8 was widened in the same phase so these authored files are still swept for non-ASCII bytes and disallowed email-shaped tokens; the offline composition proof is the sibling selfcheck-routing.mjs.
repo_note: The session cwd, and nothing more. run-e2e.mjs uses this only as `cwd = args.cwd || REPO` for the spawn, so it must be an EXISTING readable directory that all three arms see IDENTICALLY; this suite grades answer prose and reads no target file, so its contents are irrelevant to the metric. Relative, so it is machine-independent: it resolves against the invoking process's cwd, and every documented invocation runs from the repo root (pass --cwd to override). The prompts dir is chosen because it is the LEAST informative existing directory available -- it holds only the nine questions themselves, and reading a sibling question reveals nothing about any case's expected owner. The repo ROOT was considered and REJECTED: the tracked tree carries variant A's own SKILL.md bodies under plugins/lz-tdd/ plus this phase's planning documents, which state the expected owner per case, so a session that opened either would contaminate the measurement AND silently collapse arm isolation (a variant C run could recover the narrative sections variant C removes). The suite dir itself was also rejected -- its targets.json names the corpus path, and the corpus carries expectedOwner. RESIDUAL RISK, stated rather than hidden: a session can still walk UP out of any in-repo cwd. That risk is identical across all three arms, no prompt points at a file, and every run's meta.json records a tool_calls histogram plus the routing_table_read fact, so a run that went spelunking is visible in the evidence rather than silent.
skillCommand_note: Present because run-e2e.mjs reads SUITE.skillCommand at module load, NOT because anything here force-invokes. No arm in this suite is in composePrompt's force-invoke branch: all three placement arms compose a natural prompt so the -p bytes are identical arm to arm and auto-trigger stays a shared constant (D-11). This value therefore never reaches a composed prompt, and skill_forced -- which runOne computes off the composed prompt's actual bytes rather than off the arm name -- reads false for every run by construction. The value names lz-red only because the key needs one.
trackSkills_note: All THREE shipped skills, unlike the apply suites' pair, because the metric is WHICH ONE the answer names (D-12). Tracking all three is also what makes the per-arm auto-trigger reading meaningful: with byte-identical descriptions across the arms, a difference in which skill model-fired is noise, not signal (Pitfall 3), and it cannot be seen at all unless every candidate is tracked.

preambles.recommend: You are pair-programming with me. Tell me how you would approach what I am asking. Do NOT edit any file and do NOT run any command. Here is my question:

preambles_note: ROUTING-NEUTRAL by construction, and that is the load-bearing property. It establishes only the harness constraint -- advise, do not act -- and names no skill and none of the words classify, route, routing, owner or seam. A preamble that named the task would lead all three arms EQUALLY and so would not bias the A/B, but it would destroy what the A/B measures: the question is whether the loaded body makes the model reach the right destination unprompted, and a preamble that asks for a destination answers it for the model. The shared default is overridden rather than reused because the default opens with 'Read what I point you at', and no prompt in this corpus points at anything. The override is per SUITE, never per arm, so prompt parity across the three arms is unaffected.
prompts_note: Nine entries whose ids are EXACTLY the nine ids in tools/rgr-cases.json, one prompt file per case, each derived from that case's `request` field. The corpus is the single source and this is the derived consumer; a divergence between the guard's corpus and the eval's prompts would be a silent MEASUREMENT error rather than a cosmetic one, which is why selfcheck-routing.mjs asserts the id-for-id correspondence. No entry declares `code`, so apply mode selects none of them -- this suite is recommend-only and the graded artifact is answer.md.
